text:
maria (security-engineer): quick sanity check — we're planning a KEK swap for prod envelopes next wed 02:00 UTC. goal: move all envelopes from KEK v3 -> KEK v4 with minimal impact. iking for any gotchas re: cross-kms, audit logs, or RBAC changes.

ajay (eng-crypto): +1 good idea to run a small canary first. note: AWS KMS has ReEncrypt which we can use, GCP needs unwrap/wrap with CryptoKeyVersions, Azure uses unwrapKey/wrapKey. behavior and quotas differ.

linda (platform): canary sounds good. what's the scope? entire DB or just objects in s3? how many envelopes approx?

maria (security-engineer): ~12M envelopes across s3 + postgres metadata. plan: fanout worker that reads metadata cursor, pulls envelope header (enc DEK), calls KMS rewrap, writes new header and checkpoint. batch size default 500.

tom (sre): watch regional KMS quota. we've seen throttle spikes on reEncrypt calls if we blast a single region. recommend per-region rate limiter + global token bucket.

ajay (eng-crypto): also ensure the service principal has both Decrypt (or ReEncrypt) and Encrypt on the destination key. For AWS IAM: kms:ReEncrypt*, kms:DescribeKey. For GCP: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on both key versions. For Azure: key unwrap/wrap permissions. RBAC change needs approval from infra-admins.

maria (security-engineer): noted about RBAC. we need an auditable role change — adding svc-kek-swap@prod as iam member. can someone draft the policy statement?

linda (platform): I'll open the iam PR. policy will be limited to a single key ARN per region and only for the swap window. also add condition: aws:RequestTag/operation = "kek-swap" so we can filter audit logs.

ajay (eng-crypto): audit logging: ensure CloudTrail / CloudAuditLogs capture ReEncrypt/Encrypt/Decrypt and that logs are forwarded to SIEM with envelope id in the log context. we should also emit app-level audit events with old_key_id/new_key_id per envelope.

tom (sre): suggest metrics: processed/sec, rewrap-errors/sec, throttle-rate, last-checkpoint-ts, percent-complete. create Grafana dashboard and alerts: >5% error or sustained throttle >1s p50 increase should page oncall.

maria (security-engineer): failing items plan: move to DLQ with error-code, error-message, retry_count, last-error-ts. DLQ is a separate SQS topic + table for manual remediation.

ajay (eng-crypto): handling errors: transient throttling -> exponential backoff with full jitter, permanent crypto errors (InvalidCiphertext, KMSAccessDenied) -> DLQ. keep idempotency: store change under a new envelope_version and use CAS on metadata to avoid races.

linda (platform): checkpointing: commit cursor every 1000 envelopes or every 30s whichever first. add a secondary progress table: job_id, processed_count, failed_count, last_key_version. This helps resume after crash.

maria (security-engineer): canary plan: 1k envelopes in us-east-1, run at 10% of intended throughput. validate outputs with checksum and attempt reads from services using new KEK.

ajay (eng-crypto): pseudo-code for worker (keeps it simple):
```python
for batch in cursor(batching=500):
  for env in batch:
    try:
      rewrap = kms.reencrypt(CiphertextBlob=env.wrap, DestinationKeyId=new_kek)
      update_metadata(env.id, wrap=rewrap, kek_version=new_ver)
    except ThrottlingException:
      retry_with_exponential_backoff(env)
    except PermanentKmsError as e:
      dlq.push(env.id, err=str(e))
  checkpoint(batch.last_id)
```

tom (sre): add logging around request IDs and KMS requestID so we can match provider logs to our app logs. send those to the SIEM as well.

linda (platform): operational controls: throttler settings per region, "graceful-drain" endpoint to pause new work, and a manual override to reduce concurrency. also add canary flag so we can route only sample envelopes.

ajay (eng-crypto): data plane considerations: if using customer-managed keys in customer clouds (Private deployments) we need to ensure the operator has no ability to see DEKs. recommended pattern: use KMS ReEncrypt when possible (provider-side), otherwise worker must decrypt DEK locally only in memory and rewrap immediately, zeroing memory after. document in runbook.

maria (security-engineer): about compliance: capture old_key_id/new_key_id + timestamp + actor in audit events. retention: keep audit records for 7 years for regulated customers. link to runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/kek-swap (draft).

tom (sre): chaos test suggestion: simulate KMS throttling and partial network partitions to ensure we don't double-write or corrupt envelopes. run on staging first.

linda (platform): rollout strat: canary -> ramp 1%/5%/25%/100% with 30m dwell and success gates. automate rollback: if rewrap-errors > 1% in window -> pause and revert to previous checkpoint behavior.

ajay (eng-crypto): one more gotcha: some envelopes were wrapped with legacy algorithm (RSA-OAEP variants) — ensure rewrap worker recognizes and handles algorithm migration, or DLQ those for manual handling.

maria (security-engineer): thanks — I'll schedule the canary and send PR for RBAC. final checklist in thread so we don't miss anything:
- canary job created and scoped (linda)
- IAM policy PR (linda)
- runbook + audit mapping (maria)
- Grafana dashboard + alerts (tom)
- DLQ schema + remediation flow (linda)
- cryptography handling for legacy wraps (ajay)

linda (platform): working on iam PR now. assigning reviewers.

ajay (eng-crypto): i'll add detection for legacy wraps and a converter tool prototype.

maria (security-engineer): great. once canary passes I'll announce schedule and open the migration job. ping me if you spot anything missing. :thumbsup: 

deploy-bot: deployment 2026.03.21-7ff3 started by linda (platform) — canary-worker:v2 -> staging (ETA 2m).

tom (sre): watching logs, will report if throttle > threshold.

maria (security-engineer): last note: ensure ENVELOPE_ID is in every log line for easier forensics. thanks all.
